mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is held constant above 5% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 forward 60-day return tends to be negative due to persistent higher real borrowing costs compressing corporate credit spreads and equity discount rates.
failure_condition: Over a 60-day horizon, SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from a zero-move baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during qualifying periods.

mechanism_narrative: An unexpected monthly increase in unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in hourly wage growth (indirect proxy via UNRATE) predicts negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns as investor sentiment deteriorates on labor market weakness.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month AND UNRATE < previous month
failure_condition: During triggered events, SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in retail sales ( proxy via HOUST ) of at least 3% for three consecutive months is associated with a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return as it signals resilient consumer demand and upward earnings revisions.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > previous month AND HOUST > previous previous month AND HOUST > previous previous previous month
failure_condition: Over 20 days following qualifying HOUST surge, SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 5% followed by a rebound of at least 8% within the next two months predicts a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as it reflects cyclical supply-chain normalization and upward earnings expectations.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month AND INDPRO < previous previous month AND INDPRO > previous+2 month by > 8%
failure_condition: During qualifying INDPRO cycles, SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than the prior 60-day average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the annualized CPIAUCSL inflation rate exceeds 4% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return tends to be negative as investors anticipate rate hikes that erode equity valuations.
failure_condition: During inflation spikes, SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in unemployment (UNRATE) below 3.5% followed by a sustained rise in job openings (implied via labor market momentum) predicts a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as it signals labor market tightness and upward earnings momentum.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 3.5 for one month AND UNRATE > 3.5 for the next two months
failure_condition: During such UNRATE regimes, SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly declines in consumer confidence ( proxy via indirect market-based sentiment proxies not available; instead, use a proxy for retail sales momentum via HOUST ) of 10% or more are associated with negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns due to risk-off sentiment.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < previous month AND HOUST < previous previous month AND HOUST < previous previous previous month
failure_condition: During such declines, SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 2-month decline in manufacturing activity (INDPRO) followed by two months of flat or modest growth predicts a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as it suggests a bottoming-out in supply-side constraints and improved earnings outlook.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month AND INDPRO < previous previous month AND INDPRO >= previous+2 month
failure_condition: During qualifying INDPRO patterns, SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than the prior 60-day average (t-test p > 0.05).
